lines: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness, it was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity.
It is a far, far better thing that I do, than I have ever done; it is a far, far better rest that I go to than I have ever known.
I have already said, that for my prospering there, I am sensible I may be indebted to you, sir. For the rest, it is my Refuge.
I am going to see his Ghost! It will be his Ghost--not him!
I am not a shoemaker by trade? No, I was not a shoemaker by trade. I-I learnt it here. I taught myself.
Miss Manette, I am a man of business. I have a business charge to acquit myself of.
I am a Briton, I am desperate. I don’t care an English Twopence for myself.
Speak for yourself, Mr. Lorry; I have a night’s work to do yet. Speak for yourself.
Perfectly so, madame. She is going to be married.
Saying your prayers! You’re a nice woman! What do you mean by flopping yourself down and praying agin me?
I was not praying against you; I was praying for you.
Oh, father, I should so like to be a Resurrection-Man when I’m quite growed up!
Mr. Jarvis Lorry, are you a clerk in Tellson’s bank?
It does not take a long time for an earthquake to swallow a town.
I choose them as real men, of my name--Jacques is my name--to whom the sight is likely to do good.
Repression is the only lasting philosophy. The dark deference of fear and slavery, my friend, will keep the dogs obedient to the whip.
Bad Fortune! And here are the tumbrils! And Evrémonde will be despatched in a wink, and she not here!
She has a fine head for it. I have seen blue eyes and golden hair there, and they looked charming when Samson held them up.
I saw him then, messieurs, a year ago this running summer, underneath the carriage of the Marquis, hanging by the chain.
I mind nothing while I hold your hand. I shall mind nothing when I let it go, if they are rapid.
